: 
G.A., Sumit Kumar Srivastava 
 Court No. - 12
 Hon'Ble Pankaj Bhatia, J. 
1.
Short counter affidavit filed on behalf of opposite parties no.2 and 3 is taken on record.

2. Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and Sri Manoj Kumar Tiwari holding brief of Sri Sumit K. Srivastava, learned Counsel appearing on behalf of opposite parties no.2 and 3.
3.

The applicant seeks enlargement on bail in FIR No.138 of 2024, under Sections 366, 376, 323,
506, 120-B IPC, Police Station Jethwara, District Pratapgarh.
4. Initially the FIR in question was lodged under Section 366 IPC stating that the daughter of the informant was missing and was enticed by the applicant.

Subsequently, in the statements under Sections 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C., the victim stated that she is aged about 19 years and while coming home, the applicant and the co-accused had met and sat her on a motorcycle and took her at home and committed wrong.
The medical on record does not corroborate any allegation for any injury.
5. Learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the bail prayer.

6. Considering the age of the victim and the statements of the victim recorded under Sections 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C. coupled with the fact that the applicant has no criminal antecedents and is languishing in jail since 22.07.2024, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.
